correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the first core infection, a single opposite-color seed exponential clock races one original winner-seed clock and n-2 independent two-stage gamma clocks. The integral and rational finite sum follow exactly. The weighted Laplace expansion supplies the rate-universal leading term and the evaluated second-order coefficient; conditional half-normal time and binomial residual infections imply the macroscopic split and all fixed minority moments. Separate exact-rational finite-state recursions reproduce the entire final color-count law on small instances. Limitations: proof assumes independent exponential contacts, two peripheral seeds, fixed positive rates.

value.rationale: The result quantifies the first nontrivial finite-size failure of the established winner-takes-all-but-one phenomenon in a canonical deterministic heterogeneous network. Its rate-independent square-root coefficient despite different infection speeds is structural; rare macroscopic coexistence makes the minority outbreak expectation diverge even though its size converges to one in probability, revealing the limits of typical-outcome summaries. Both the event and the invariant are naturally defined for competing infection and matter for rare-outbreak risk assessment.
